transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-11-30
- Start: 17:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alice Monroe (Redwood AE), Diego Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kramer (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Pelican CTO), Maya Chen (Pelican Sr ML Eng), Sarah Lopez (Pelican Product), Evan Park (Pelican DevOps)

Summary: quick intro, qualification on stack and constraints, discussion of free credits/time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, security concerns and pilot success metrics. Next steps defined at end.

00:00 Alice: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alice from redwood, i'm the acct exec on this one, we've got diego and jules from engineering, um quick round robin?
00:14 Rajiv: yeah hi i'm rajiv, cto at pelican insights, we're building a contextual insights layer for enterprise docs, thanks for taking the time
00:20 Maya: maya, ml eng, i'll be running the evaluation and integrating model outputs into the pipeline
00:27 Sarah: sarah product, i'll own acceptance criteria and demo for stakeholders
00:32 Alice: perfect, thanks. quick agenda — 1) understand current stack and constraints, 2) run through quickstart options (free credits, ttft), 3) talk hosting choices (hosted/dedicated/private) and security, 4) agree pilot scope and next steps
00:48 Diego: just to set expectations from the se side, we'll also flag typical perf tradeoffs — batching, kv-cash, uh kv-cache behavior — and what we do for warm starts
00:58 Rajiv: sorry what was that, kv-cash?
01:01 Diego: kv-cache sorry, auto transcript, where we keep the key value cache for transformer attention, that'll matter for latency when you do long context sessions
01:10 Sarah: underlined, thanks.
01:12 Alice: maybe start with stack — what are you running now?
01:16 Rajiv: infra is aws, primarily ecs and sagemaker for training. serving is kubernetes on EKS for internal microservices, but for model inference we don't want to self-host initially — we prefer quick experiment on a hosted api to iterate fast
01:28 Maya: yeah we do all training in-house; for serving evaluating hosted first, then we might go dedicated if we need predictable throughput and lower unit-costs or private for data residency reasons
01:38 Alice: that's a common path, self-serve/credits to ttft then evaluate dedicated or private. what's your timeline?
01:45 Rajiv: 6-8 weeks to pilot decision, aim to ship an initial feature in Q1. need to know TTFT and cost to provision budget.
01:56 Alice: perfect. on free credits — we can provision a credits pack that lets you run a 2-week pilot on hosted. it includes X tokens / Y embeddings, and we can increase if you need. that should get you to first meaningful demo in days not weeks
02:12 Maya: good. how long is TTFT if i hand this to an engineer — from signup to first request?
02:18 Alice: typically under an hour for a dev who's done API keys before — if you use our SDK quickstart and the sample docker. diego, can you explain typical path?
02:26 Diego: yeah. sign-up, create API key, pick model, call /v1/generate. we have SDKs in python and node. samples in repo — with our quickstart and pre-populated prompts, most teams get first successful call in 10-30 minutes. if you need streaming or function calling it's still pretty quick, 30-90 minutes for an app prototype
02:46 Maya: any infra changes on our side?
02:49 Diego: no infra changes required for hosted. for dedicated you'll want to set up peering or private link and we can do VPC peering or a private endpoint, and for private on-prem we'd coordinate a package deployment — that takes longer, like weeks depending on network and approvals
03:06 Evan: on peering, do you support AWS Privatelink?
03:09 Diego: yes, we support PrivateLink and VPC peering, and we have an option for customer-managed NAT and routing for Private deployment.
03:16 Rajiv: security — are you SOC2 and do you have KMS integration?
03:21 Alice: we are SOC 2 compliant, we have customer keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; hosted also supports envelope encryption with managed keys. i'll send the security pack after this call
03:33 Sarah: do you have SSO / SAML?
03:36 Alice: yes enterprise SSO, SAML and OIDC, RBAC in the console, and audit logs per token or per route in the console.
03:46 Maya: any concerns about PII in the prompts? we do have legal constraints on extracting sensitive fields from docs
03:52 Diego: two levers — routing and retention. hosted sandbox keeps minimal logs for the credits pilot, and we can enable automatic redaction or not persist kv-cache across sessions; private deployment gives you full control over data residency and logs
04:08 Rajiv: cost question — for hosted quickstart, do you provide cost estimates? we care about tokens per inference and average length
04:15 Alice: yes we'll run an initial cost projection after you share a sample of your expected prompt lengths and QPS. diego will share a benchmark harness you can run against your prompt templates to estimate unit cost at scale
04:28 Diego: benchmark harness will include simulated request patterns and a small docker image so you can run locally or in your cluster against our endpoint, capturing p50/p95 latency and tokens per call
04:39 Maya: what's the default model, are we restricted to redwood-curated models?
04:43 Alice: you can choose from our catalog; hosted has a set of recommended models for lower latency and better cost. we also support bringing your own model in private/dedicated in some cases, but that often requires onboarding and validation
04:58 Rajiv: for the pilot, what would success look like?
05:02 Sarah: from product side — stable responses and < 500ms p95 for simple classification, plus a demo-ready integration in the app.
05:11 Maya: from eng — reproducible latency profile, ability to scale to 50 rps with acceptable cost, and no leakage of customer PII in logs.
05:20 Rajiv: for execs — predictable pricing and a path to a dedicated contract if this proves out
05:27 Alice: sounds good. so pilot scope proposal — 2-week hosted pilot using credits, run benchmark harness on your prompts, integrate SDK into a dev branch to demo UI, security pack enabled, short retention and redaction for logs. after pilot, review metrics: latency, cost, quality. if throughput or cost requires, evaluate dedicated reserved capacity. if data residency prevents hosted, discuss private deployment timeline.
05:50 Rajiv: that aligns. what are the limits on the credits pack? like tokens and concurrency?
05:56 Alice: we typically give enough tokens for Xk generations and Yk embeddings; concurrency is soft-limited on hosted but we'll prioritize pilot traffic and can open burst capacity. specifics we'll include in the onboarding note
06:09 Maya: any throttling we should be aware of for streaming responses? sometimes we rely on server-sent events in the app
06:15 Diego: streaming supported; depending on model and region you might see slightly higher latency under high concurrency. we'll include guidance on batching and response chunking to minimize perceived latency in the UI
06:28 Evan: network egress — if we run tests from our VPC to your hosted endpoints, do you bill egress?
06:34 Alice: hosted API usage includes our token pricing; network egress is billed by your cloud provider. for dedicated we can colocate in same region or peering to reduce egress costs
06:44 Maya: any gotchas with auth for quickstart? service accounts?
06:47 Alice: for quickstart you'll get a root api key for the credit pool and can create scoped keys; for production use we recommend short-lived keys and service account integration with your secrets manager.
06:58 Jules: i'll add, we also provide sample middleware to rotate keys if you're using our SDKs, and example env var patterns for containerized apps
07:08 Rajiv: great. can you walk me through an example curl request and expected response times?
07:14 Diego: sure. example: POST /v1/generate with model: redwood-llama-lite, body with prompt and max_tokens. for simple prompts we commonly see 80-150ms p50 and 250-600ms p95 depending on size; for longer contexts or function calls it can be higher. note these are approximate — we'll run the harness for your patterns
07:40 Maya: when you say dedicated reduces unit cost, what's the ballpark?
07:44 Alice: Dedicated has lower per-token billing because of reserved GPU capacity and better packing; typical customers see 20-50% lower unit cost depending on utilization. we'll tailor an estimate once we see your QPS/year and prompt profile
07:58 Rajiv: if we land on dedicated, what's the lead time?
08:02 Diego: provisioning a dedicated pool is days to a couple of weeks depending on capacity and region. private on-prem can be multiple weeks with network and security approvals.
08:12 Sarah: for our procurement, we need a one-pager of pricing and terms for the pilot and how the transition to dedicated billing works
08:19 Alice: will do. i'll attach the pilot pricing sheet and an example dedicated contract transition clause.
08:25 Evan: how do rollback or fallbacks work if a model is down?
08:29 Diego: we have smart routing and fallbacks — you can set a policy to route to a lower-cost or lower-latency model if the primary fails. failover is automatic, and we keep trace logs to debug any mismatched outputs
08:44 Rajiv: you mentioned KV cache — is there a recommended cache size or behaviour for our use case? we're doing context snippets of 2-4k tokens
08:52 Diego: for 2-4k contexts you want to tune your KV sharding and not keep very long-lived caches per session. for high concurrent short sessions, continuous batching helps. we'll add recommended defaults in the benchmark docs
09:10 Maya: what about model updates? we have strict requirements that model changes be governed and evaluated for regressions
09:15 Alice: our rollout supports pinned versions and canary deploys; Redwood Optimize will flag quality regressions against your eval set and we can hold rollouts until approved
09:26 Sarah: nice. as for compliance, do you provide audit logs that we can ship to our SIEM?
09:31 Alice: yes: audit events, request/response metadata (not plaintext of responses unless configured) and you can stream logs to S3 or to SIEM via our log forwarding integration
09:41 Rajiv: ok that's promising. any reasons customers fail the pilot?
09:45 Diego: usually mismatched expectations — either prompt design yields noisy outputs or the sample dataset for eval is not representative. also sometimes teams underestimate integration time in the app — we help with templates to speed that up
09:57 Sarah: ok what are the typical integration pitfalls?
09:59 Maya: rate limiting and tokenization surprises — some tokens count more than expected which bumps cost.
10:05 Diego: yes also batching too aggressively can harm latency; you need workload tuning. we provide suggested batching configs per workload type
10:16 Rajiv: can you support a trial where we run traffic from our staging environment and hit your hosted endpoint? we want production-like networking to test latency
10:24 Alice: absolutely — we'll whitelist staging IPs and prioritize pilot traffic for the credit pool. just share the egress IP ranges and diego will open burst capacity for the test window
10:35 Evan: regarding VPC peering if we go dedicated later, what data path is used? is traffic egress in our control?
10:41 Diego: with VPC peering traffic stays within aws backbone if in same region; PrivateLink gives more control and lower egress. for private deployments you'll keep data inside your network entirely
10:53 Sarah: ok great, for the pilot timeline — can we map milestones?
10:57 Alice: proposed: week 0 - onboarding + credits + sample harness; week 1 - run benchmarks and integrate SDK into dev branch; week 2 - polish demo, collect metrics and decision review. that's two weeks total
11:12 Rajiv: good. i'd like to add an acceptance metric: p95 < 600ms for classification and synthetic recall > 0.85 on our eval set
11:20 Sarah: and acceptance means greenlit for dedicated evaluation if cost projections under target
11:25 Alice: noted. diego, anything else to add on benchmarks?
11:29 Diego: we'll include a small script to vary concurrency and batch sizes; it outputs p50/p95 and token counts to a csv you can upload. also a docker image so you don't have to fiddle with deps
11:40 Maya: can we bring our own model v checkpoints later? for private or dedicated
11:44 Diego: yes, BYOM is supported in private and in some dedicated cases but we do a validation pass — will need to check compatibility with our runtime and kernels, especially quantized variants
11:55 Rajiv: how are rollouts for BYOM handled? we worry about perf regressions
11:59 Alice: similar controls — pinned versions, traffic split, and Redwood Optimize monitors quality regressions against golden evals
12:08 Sarah: ok, small question: do you support streaming embeddings or batch only?
12:12 Diego: embeddings API supports both synchronous batch endpoints and streaming in the newer SDKs; the quickstart uses sync calls for simplicity
12:20 Rajiv: do you have any examples of customers that started hosted then moved to dedicated for cost reasons?
12:25 Alice: yes, several fintech and retail customers follow that path — we can share anonymized case studies in the pack
12:31 Maya: one operational thing — retention by default for pilot is minimal, right? we need zero persisted text for legal
12:36 Alice: for the credits sandbox we can set retention to minimal and redact obvious PII; for strict legal needs you'd want private deployment or dedicated with customer-managed keys
12:46 Evan: on billing — pilot credits are free, how is overage handled?
12:49 Alice: we'll notify you if you bump past the pool; you can opt into additional paid credits or pause the trial. overages not charged without a named PO
12:58 Rajiv: great. can you also include sample SAML metadata docs for our IdP?
13:03 Alice: yes i'll include SAML metadata and the console setup guide
13:08 Sarah: ok wrapping up, are there any blockers from our side?
13:12 Rajiv: we'll need internal ok on data usage but we can start engineering work while legal reviews. i'll confirm stakeholders and timeline by next week
13:20 Maya: i'll start pulling the top 20 prompts and a small eval set to share
13:24 Alice: awesome. recap of next steps: we'll send security pack, benchmark harness, onboarding doc and credits. you'll share prompts, IP ranges, and internal decision timeline. then schedule a 30 min deep dive week of Dec 14th
13:40 Rajiv: sounds good. thanks everyone
13:42 Alice: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links
14:00 (call end)

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors (kv-cash / kv-cache), speaker overlaps, filler words. The squad also requested a dockerized harness and sample curl examples.
